description:
FILED s450v (Opus round 9 agent V), from the #520/#521 probes.  PRE-EXISTING.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3):

    my $r = \"Z"; my $x = "mAn"; $x =~ s/A/${$r}/; print "$x\n";
        perl  mZn
        PCL   mn
    PCL_OPT=-raw-slot ./runpcl <same file>   ->  mZn      <-- the discriminator

CAUSE: the raw-slot pass demotes `$r` to a raw STRING slot --
`(let (($r (%pcl-to-string-strict (p-backslash "Z") "$r"))) ...)` -- because the
only other use of `$r` is inside the s/// replacement, and the verdict scan does
not see a DEREF spelling there.  `(p-cast-$ $r)` then symbolically dereferences
the string "SCALAR(0x...)" and gets undef.

WHICH SPELLINGS (probed, all with the variable used ONLY in the replacement):

    s/A/${$r}/     WRONG (empty)      s/A/$h->{k}/    right
    s/A/$$r/       WRONG (empty)      s/A/$ar->[1]/   right
    s/A/@{$ar}/    WRONG (empty)

so it is the DEREF spellings (`${...}`, `$$name`, `@{...}`), which are exactly
the ones the replacement re-parses as a source FRAGMENT (StringInterpolation's
_interp_reparse).  A use of the same variable ANYWHERE ELSE in the sub (even
`my $keep = $$r;`) makes the verdict right again, which is the confirming probe.

SHAPE OF A FIX: the raw-slot verdict must read the replacement's references
through the same scanner the emission does (Pl::InterpScan), not a name match --
or, cheaper and safe, treat any variable named inside an s/// replacement whose
event form is 'deref'/'expr' as a non-raw use.  Probe the m// pattern side too:
`"$$r"` in a plain dq string is RIGHT today, so the hole may be specific to the
replacement's fragment path.

BAR: the five spellings above vs perl, with and without PCL_OPT=-raw-slot; rows
in Pl/t/regexp-subst-01.t or the passes guard.
subject: SILENT WRONG: the `raw-slot` verdict is BLIND to a DEREF use inside an s/// replacement -- `my $r = \"Z"; $x =~ s/A/${$r}/` writes the EMPTY string
